newsitem.title: UK: UK may relax "watershed" rules for pay-per-view TV.
newsitem.headline: UK may relax "watershed" rules for pay-per-view TV.

text.p: Restrictions on when television programmes can be screened may be relaxed for new cable and satellite pay per view services, Britain's Independent Television Commission (ITC) said on Tuesday.
"Watershed" restrictions may be relaxed providing reception is subject to a PIN number system or other mechanism to deny children access to unsuitable adult material, the ITC said.
The provision of pay per view services will be permitted under existing licences on an experimental basis and will be subject to a full review after the first such service is launched.
Pay per view is expected to play a growing role in Britain as BSkyB and cable companies launch multi-channel digital services in the next 12 months.
